# Mark Cuban on the Broken Drug Pricing System & How PBMs Really Work | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 50

First listed: 2026-03-16 | Evaluation cutoff: 2026-11-10

[Back to library](../README.md)

## Source versions

- [YouTube: Mark Cuban on the Broken Drug Pricing System & How PBMs Really Work | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 50](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gfH0jyPwSDQ) - 2026-03-16
- [Substack: Mark Cuban Shares His Plan For Fixing Drug Prices in America | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 50](https://realeismanplaybook.substack.com/p/mark-cuban-shares-his-plan-for-fixing-408) - 2026-03-16

Earliest listed publication among matched versions, not proof of an unedited contemporaneous archive. Claim timestamps refer to the reviewed version.

## Summary

Mark Cuban explains Cost Plus, PBM incentives and direct employer healthcare, while Eisman explicitly adopts several conclusions in his closing. Concentration and specialty-drug markups have primary support. The summary conflates rebates reaching plans with PBMs retaining them; the claims that PBMs exist only in America and only Cost Plus publishes pharmacy prices are contradicted. Company savings, retaliation and healthcare reform claims largely lack matched causal evidence. Cuban’s cash position and flow-driven equity theory remain guest views.

Material drug-pricing critique has empirical support, but several adopted premises are overstated. No investment-return win is inferred from business-model praise. Regulatory allegations are distinguished from established universal causation.

- [Proposed Express Scripts settlement to change drug pricing practices](https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2026/02/ftc-secures-landmark-settlement-express-scripts-lower-drug-costs-american-patients) (2026-02-04): Proposed consent package changes standard formularies, net-cost patient payments, compensation linkage and disclosures, and offers sponsors a transition away from rebate guarantees/spread pricing. - [UnitedHealth Group third-quarter 2026 results](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/731766/000073176626000255/earningsrelease3q26unh.htm) (2026-10-13): Q3 Optum Health operating earnings $735m versus $41m, margin 3.2% versus 0.2%; adjusted margin 2.6%. Insight earnings $1.279bn versus $920m and Rx $1.718bn versus $1.549bn. Prior periods are recast for Optum Financial. Results show recovery, not uniform segment earnings decline; restructuring and valuation adjustments remain relevant.
- [Alignment Healthcare third-quarter 2026 results](https://ir.alignmenthealth.com/news-releases/news-release-details/alignment-healthcare-reports-third-quarter-2026-results-updates) (2026-10-29): Revenue grew 36.7%, membership 31.2%; adjusted EBITDA fell 32.8% to $21.8m, margin 1.6%, with $8.1m net loss. Medical benefits ratio rose 240bp to 89.5%; full-year profit guidance was reduced despite higher revenue guidance. Nine-month net income still increased, so this is a quarter of pressure, not proven model failure.
- [Molina third-quarter 2026 results](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1179929/000117992926000042/moh3q26_er.htm) (2026-10-21): Q3 adjusted EPS $0.89 versus $1.84, nine-month $4.74 versus $13.49; MCR 92.9%. Adjusted full-year guidance at least $5.25. Persistent margin pressure supports slow recovery; management also sees possible Medicaid turning point.

## Framework and tools

- Map payments among patients, plans, manufacturers and intermediaries before attributing profits.
- Strong concrete mechanism questions, followed by insufficient challenge to categorical guest assertions.
- Closing paraphrase can become stronger than what the guest actually said.
- Patient cost and manufacturer list price are different benchmarks.

Tools and charts discussed, not a complete visual inspection:

- Hypothetical $1000 drug and $400 rebate waterfall
- Deductible affordability examples
- Cost-plus markup comparison
- Employer formulary and network access
- Public-company count and retirement fund flows

## Source cautions

Dialogue context identifies Mark Cuban as guest. Host closing is clearly Eisman and supplies explicit adoption; earlier questions alone do not. Market allocation and entrepreneurial forecasts remain Cuban views.
- Ads around 18:30-22:15 excluded.
- ASR brand spelling in the Stelara biosimilar example is uncertain; annual versus per-dose prices are not directly comparable.
- Guest corrects always cheaper to almost always cheaper.
- Closing rebate-retention description differs from guest employer-pass-through explanation.
